chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Absent from the jazz books: Nat Hentoff's omission
summary: Willard says no jazz reference books mention Collins; he complains Hentoff wrote about Scoops Carey yet left him out despite longer tenures with Tatum and Roy.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: We've been here looking through a stack of jazz books, and a stack of records (inaudible). It's rather upsetting. In all of the books that we found, you don't find any reference to John Collins. Yet there's a rather detailed personnel of bands that you played in. Isn't that strange?
Yes, it's amazing. I was looking in Nat Hentoff's book here. Here is a man that is supposed to

have a comprehensive book here, of you know, jazz. Okay? He's gone all through Chicago, New York, he has skirted around me with -- he's talking about Scoops Carey at length, with Art Tatum. I worked with Art Tatum with the same band, worked with Art Tatum longer than Scoops. I worked with Roy Eldridge longer than Scoops, I worked with him longer than Zutty. How can a man write a comprehensive report of jazz, a history of jazz, and exclude me like this. It's amazing.
Well, I -- I just happened to mention him, but I have made -- if I've made one recording I've made thousands of recordings.

I have solos. I sold with Art. I have solos. I've worked with Nat Cole, I worked with Nat Cole for 14 years. I worked with Prez, I worked with Fletcher, I -- and I mean this is a matter of record. I have recorded with Prez, recorded with Lady Day. How is this possible?
It was one of the things we're doing now is trying to set the record straight.
It's just amazing, and it's very up-setting because I -- there is not a musician of any worth in the world, I would say, I would say a jazz musician, and
